questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Subsurface Soil Exploration, Boring Methods, Standard Penetration Test, Cone Penetration Test
questions.text: Describe the Standard Penetration Test (SPT) procedure according to IS 2131. Explain: (a) Overburden Pressure Correction ($N' = N \times C_N$), and (b) Dilatancy Correction ($N'' = 15 + \frac{1}{2}(N' - 15)$ for submerged fine sand/silt). Calculate corrected $N$-value if observed blow counts at $6\,\text{m}$ depth are $18, 23, 17$ in submerged sand with $\gamma_{sat} = 19\,\text{kN/m}^3$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Deep Foundations
questions.text: Explain Apparent Earth Pressure Envelopes (Peck's Envelopes) for deep braced cuts in: (a) Dense sand, (b) Soft-to-medium clay, and (c) Stiff fissured clay. Determine strut loads at levels A, B, and C for an excavation of depth $10\,\text{m}$ with strut spacing $2.5\,\text{m}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Deep Foundations
questions.text: What is a Sheet Pile? Draw clear deflected shapes and pressure distributions for: (a) Cantilever sheet pile wall in sand, (b) Anchored bulkhead with free earth support, and (c) Anchored bulkhead with fixed earth support. Prove that anchor placement reduces required depth of embedment.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Settlement of Shallow Foundations
questions.text: Differentiate between General Shear Failure, Local Shear Failure, and Punching Shear Failure with neat sketches and stress-strain / settlement curves.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Bearing Capacity of Shallow Foundations
questions.text: State Terzaghi's Ultimate Bearing Capacity equations for strip, square, and circular footings. Explain modifications for: (a) Local shear failure ($c' = \frac{2}{3}c, \tan\phi' = \frac{2}{3}\tan\phi$), and (b) Water Table correction factor $R_w$ when water table is above, at, and below the footing base.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Design of Raft/Mat Foundations & Combined Footings
questions.text: Explain the concept of Fully Compensated (Floating) Raft Foundation. Derive the formula for required depth of foundation: $D_f = \frac{Q}{A \cdot \gamma}$. When is a mat foundation chosen over individual isolated footings?

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Deep Foundations
questions.text: Classify Pile Foundations based on: (a) Load transfer mechanism (End-bearing vs Friction piles), (b) Materials (Timber, Precast concrete, Steel), and (c) Installation method (Driven vs Bored cast-in-situ).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Deep Foundations
questions.text: Describe Negative Skin Friction in piles: its causes, effects, and calculation for single piles ($Q_{nf} = P L_c \alpha c_u$) and pile groups in consolidating clay strata.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Well Foundations & Caissons for Bridges
questions.text: Draw a neat cross-sectional sketch of a Well Foundation (Caisson) for a bridge pier. Label all components: Cutting edge, Well curb, Steining, Bottom plug, Sand filling, Top plug, and Well cap. Explain causes and remedial measures for Tilt and Shift.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Subsurface Soil Exploration, Boring Methods, Standard Penetration Test, Cone Penetration Test
questions.text: What are the different soil sampler design parameters? Define Area Ratio ($A_r = \frac{D_2^2 - D_1^2}{D_1^2} \times 100\%$), Inside Clearance ($C_i = \frac{D_3 - D_1}{D_1} \times 100\%$), and Outside Clearance ($C_o$). Explain their physical significance in obtaining undisturbed soil samples.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Design of Raft/Mat Foundations & Combined Footings
questions.text: State assumptions and limitations of Rankine's earth pressure theory. Why are retaining walls predominantly designed for Active Earth Pressure rather than Earth Pressure at Rest or Passive Earth Pressure?

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Subsurface Soil Exploration, Boring Methods, Standard Penetration Test, Cone Penetration Test
questions.text: A trapezoidal masonry retaining wall $1.0\,\text{m}$ wide at top and $3.0\,\text{m}$ wide at bottom is $4.0\,\text{m}$ high. Vertical back retains cohesionless soil ($\phi = 30^\circ$) at a surcharge angle of $20^\circ$. Using Coulomb's theory, determine maximum and minimum base pressure and check safety against sliding and overturning ($\gamma_{soil} = 20\,\text{kN/m}^3, \gamma_{masonry} = 24\,\text{kN/m}^3, \delta = 24^\circ$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Settlement of Shallow Foundations
questions.text: Explain Immediate (Elastic) Settlement and Primary Consolidation Settlement calculation of footings on clay: $S_c = \frac{C_c H_0}{1 + e_0} \log_{10}\left(\frac{\sigma_0' + \Delta\sigma'}{\sigma_0'}\right)$. What are permissible total and differential settlement limits according to IS 1904?

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Deep Foundations
questions.text: Why are dynamic pile driving formulas (e.g. Engineering News formula, Hiley's formula) unreliable for cohesive clays? Explain the Static Pile Capacity formula: $Q_{up} = c_b N_c A_b + \alpha \bar{c}_u A_s$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Deep Foundations
questions.text: Determine the allowable capacity of a $4 \times 4$ group of $40\,\text{cm}$ diameter driven concrete piles spaced at $2.5 B$ in layered sand ($3\,\text{m}$ loose sand $\phi=30^\circ$, $6\,\text{m}$ medium sand $\phi=35^\circ$, $5\,\text{m}$ dense sand $\phi=40^\circ$) with factor of safety $2.5$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Deep Foundations
questions.text: A group of 16 piles arranged in a $4 \times 4$ square grid is proportioned in soft saturated clay ($c_u = 40\,\text{kN/m}^2$). Piles are square with side $30\,\text{cm}$ and length $12\,\text{m}$. Determine center-to-center spacing for $100\%$ group efficiency (adhesion factor $\alpha = 0.8$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Subsurface Soil Exploration, Boring Methods, Standard Penetration Test, Cone Penetration Test
questions.text: A concrete gravity retaining wall of height $6\,\text{m}$ retains two soil layers: top layer of $2\,\text{m}$ ($c = 0, \phi = 32^\circ, \gamma = 18\,\text{kN/m}^3$) and bottom layer of $4\,\text{m}$ ($c = 30\,\text{kN/m}^2, \phi = 27^\circ, \gamma_{sat} = 22\,\text{kN/m}^3$) with water table at $2\,\text{m}$ depth. Draw active pressure distribution and calculate total thrust.

questions.text: What is Soil Arching? What are the essential requirements for arching effect to come into play in deep excavations and tunnels?

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Deep Foundations
questions.text: Find the required depth of embedment for an anchored sheet pile wall supporting an $8.0\,\text{m}$ deep excavation in cohesionless soil with water table at $2.5\,\text{m}$ depth. Find tensile force $T$ per meter in the anchor rod.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Subsurface Soil Exploration, Boring Methods, Standard Penetration Test, Cone Penetration Test
questions.text: A strip footing of width $2.0\,\text{m}$ carries a safe load of $400\,\text{kN/m}$ at depth $1.2\,\text{m}$ in sand ($\gamma = 16.8\,\text{kN/m}^3, \gamma_{sat} = 19.5\,\text{kN/m}^3, N_c = 58, N_q = 41, N_\gamma = 42$). Determine the Factor of Safety against shear failure when: (i) Water table is at $4.0\,\text{m}$ below GL, (ii) Water table is at $2.5\,\text{m}$ below GL, (iii) Water table rises to $0.5\,\text{m}$ below GL.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Bearing Capacity of Shallow Foundations
questions.text: A square footing $4\,\text{m} \times 4\,\text{m}$ supports a vertical column load of $2000\,\text{kN}$ acting with an eccentricity of $0.3\,\text{m}$ in one direction. What should be the minimum depth of foundation in sand ($\phi = 35^\circ, \gamma = 18\,\text{kN/m}^3, N_c = 55, N_q = 40, N_\gamma = 45$) to ensure Factor of Safety $\ge 2.5$ using Meyerhof's effective area method?

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Subsurface Soil Exploration, Boring Methods, Standard Penetration Test, Cone Penetration Test
questions.text: A mat foundation of size $18\,\text{m} \times 22\,\text{m}$ in plan has its base at $3.0\,\text{m}$ below the surface in a clay deposit ($\gamma = 20\,\text{kN/m}^3, q_u = 75\,\text{kN/m}^2$). Factor of safety against bearing failure is $3.0$. Determine total safe load of building plus raft the soil can support.
